question.problem:
| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |

Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{30}$ be a random sample of size $n=30$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.2).$

*Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ | $\,0.2643\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3050\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ | $\,0.2981\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=30,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =-2\cdot 0.3+(-1)\cdot 0.2+0\cdot 0.1+2\cdot 0.4 \\  & =-0.6-0.2+0+0.8 \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =((-2)^{2}\cdot 0.3+(-1)^{2}\cdot 0.2+{0}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.4)-{0}^{2} \\  & =(1.2+0.2+0+1.6)-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0,\frac{3}{30}) \\  & ∼N(0,0.1).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.2).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.2) & =P(\overset{―}{X}<-0.2)+P(\overset{―}{X}>0.2) \\  & ≈P(Z<\frac{-0.2-0}{\sqrt{0.1}})+P(Z>\frac{0.2-0}{\sqrt{0.1}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-0.63)+P(Z>0.63) \\  & =P(Z<-0.63)+1-P(Z<0.63) \\  & =1+Φ(-0.63)-Φ(0.63).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.63)=0.2643.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, by the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\,Φ(0.63)=1-Φ(-0.63).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.2) & =1+Φ(-0.63)-Φ(0.63) \\  & =2Φ(-0.63) \\  & =2\cdot 0.2643 \\  & =0.5286.\end{aligned}
$$
